impact.affected_asset: The admin user's image/gif badge, including the challenge flag embedded in the returned bytes.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause an admin-cookie-bearing bot to navigate to a chosen localhost optimizer URL and later read the same optimizer URL without the admin session.
impact.security_effect: Disclosure of session-derived, secret-bearing badge bytes to an unauthenticated requester through a cached optimizer response.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker can submit a syntactically valid URL in HACKER IP to POST /api/report; the route invokes bot.visit with that value.

The bot creates a localhost-scoped session cookie whose sealed data names admin before navigating to the submitted URL. The organizer solution submits a localhost image-optimizer URL whose source is /api/me/badge.

The official sequence waits after the bot navigation and then makes an unauthenticated request for the identical optimizer URL, evidencing that an optimizer representation generated in the privileged navigation is retrievable across the session boundary. The bundle does not establish the framework-internal cache-key implementation.

The badge endpoint returns the session-selected user's badge bytes as image/gif, whereas no resolved user receives 401; the solution ASCII-decodes the retrieved optimizer response and extracts a string beginning with dice{.

failure.operation: Cross-session retrieval of an image-optimizer response after privileged cache priming

primary_invariant.statement: A representation derived from a session-authenticated request to /api/me/badge must not be replayable to a requester lacking that session.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The official organizer sequence primes /_next/image?url=/api/me/badge&w=96&h=96&q=100 through an admin-cookie-bearing localhost bot navigation and subsequently retrieves the same optimizer URL as the attacker. The underlying optimizer keying and internal fetch details are not in the supplied bundle.

quality.review_notes: The official organizer solution and primary application/bot code provide a concrete reproducibility sequence and byte-level oracle. No execution transcript is supplied, so this record does not claim that the script was run. No optimizer internals, remediation patch, or regression test is supplied; cache-key construction and the precise framework-internal cause remain unverified.

remediation.invariant_restored: Optimizer responses sourced from authenticated endpoints are either not shared in a public cache or are segregated so an unauthenticated request cannot receive a representation derived using another session.
mitigation_classes: bypass caching for session-derived image sources
prevent authenticated bot navigation from priming publicly readable optimizer representations

target.component: report-driven admin bot, Next image optimizer, and session-selected badge endpoint

oracle.channel: HTTP response bytes decoded as ASCII
oracle.expected_negative: After mitigation, an unauthenticated request to the same optimizer URL must not return bytes derived from the admin session; the badge endpoint itself returns 401 when no session resolves to a user.
oracle.expected_positive: After submitting the localhost optimizer URL to /api/report and allowing the bot visit, the organizer sequence retrieves the optimizer response and finds a substring beginning with dice{ in its bytes.
